Table 3: Comprehensive evaluation results on the Agentic-MME benchmark. We evaluate tool-augmented models under two distinct interaction interfaces: Gen (Code Generation mode, where models write sandboxed Python for visual transforms) and Atm (Atomic mode, interacting via structured functioncalling APIs). Within each category, models are sorted in descending order based on their highest (Acc) across all modes. The top model in each category is highlighted with a small icon.

ImgTools: dedicated visual manipulation tools; SearchCore: open-web search is the core task; ProcessVerified: explicit process verification; Unified: protocol supports both code & function-calling for visual tools; Efficiency: cost/efficiency metric; Levels: explicit difficulty levels splits. Figure 12: Level 3 Case: Cross-Domain Multi-Hop Verification. The agent isolates a weak background logo, uses visual search to identify candidate entities, performs multi-hop web retrieval to obtain the required external fact, and then cross-validates this knowledge against another localized cue before computing the final answer.

Figure 11: Level 3 Case: Full-Image Structural Analysis for Dense Tile Estimation. The agent must infer a latent repetitive grid pattern from the full image, estimate the tile layout, and convert that estimate into a downstream numerical answer.

Figure 10: Level 3 Case: Cross-Image Spatial Grounding with Knowledge Verification. The agent first crops the map to anchor on the reference business and perform local spatial reasoning, then crops the companion street-view image to recover the road cue, and finally uses open-web retrieval to determine the associated state.
